about: Drop-in effects, systems and tools for three.js games. status: ready = copied into blocks/vendor/ and tested; reference-only = we point to the original author's repo at a pinned commit. renderer: webgl2 works with the starter; webgpu and both need three/webgpu (WebGPURenderer); 2d = plain canvas; none = not a renderer thing. See blocks/README.md.

blocks.name: Oil paint
blocks.what: Draws a three.js world as thick oil paint, dab by dab; every stroke is pinned to the world so the paint stays on things as the camera moves. Demo: a snowy ridge under an aurora, and an autumn wood, with a walking character.
blocks.good_for: A painterly third-person or first-person walking game where the look is the point; slow, calm, exploratory games.
blocks.not_for: Fast action with lots of small moving things, phones and weak laptops (heavy), or a look you want to add to an existing scene like a filter: you start from its scene.
blocks.how_to_add: node tools/blocks/add.mjs oil-paint

blocks.name: Watercolour
blocks.what: A world that starts as a pencil drawing and is painted in watercolour as you walk through it: the wash spreads from your feet, climbs the trees and stays. Demo: a wood, a stream and a meadow.
blocks.good_for: Gentle exploration games where the player "colours in" the world; storybook looks; a reveal mechanic built into the look.
blocks.not_for: Combat-heavy or fast games; games that need a hard, readable silhouette at a glance; weak hardware.
blocks.how_to_add: node tools/blocks/add.mjs watercolour

blocks.name: Coloured pencil
blocks.what: A world drawn in coloured pencil on a sketchbook page: strokes that follow each form, a second pencil for shade, a graphite outline round everything. Demo: a harbour town.
blocks.good_for: Cosy, illustrated, hand-drawn looks; town or village walking games; anything that should feel like a sketchbook.
blocks.not_for: Dark, gritty or realistic games; very fast games; weak hardware.
blocks.how_to_add: node tools/blocks/add.mjs coloured-pencil

blocks.name: Patchwork quilt
blocks.what: Makes a world out of cloth: a quilt of puffed patches with real seams and stitches, fuzzy felt, and a tilt-shift camera that sees it as a small thing on a table. Demo: a country sewn into one quilt with a rag doll.
blocks.good_for: Toy-like, handmade, miniature looks; cosy and family games; stop-motion feel.
blocks.not_for: Realistic or dark games; huge open worlds; weak hardware.
blocks.how_to_add: node tools/blocks/add.mjs patchwork-quilt

blocks.name: Painted valley
blocks.what: A summer valley in the look of hand-painted animated-film backgrounds: flat clean colour, heaped clouds, painted mountains, brush-mark meadow, and a flat-shaded inked character. Four times of day.
blocks.good_for: Bright, hopeful, hand-painted outdoor games; walking, gliding, farming or adventure games set outdoors.
blocks.not_for: Indoor, dark or realistic games; weak hardware.
blocks.how_to_add: node tools/blocks/add.mjs painted-valley

blocks.name: Slice anything
blocks.what: Cut any mesh along any plane, as many times as you like: every piece becomes a closed solid with its own Rapier body, and the cut face shows what the thing is made of (wood rings, melon seeds, marble veins).
blocks.good_for: Sword, knife and slicing games; satisfying destruction of props; physics toys.
blocks.not_for: Games that do not need cutting; huge numbers of cuts per second on weak hardware.
blocks.how_to_add: node tools/blocks/add.mjs slice-anything
blocks.notes: Uses three/webgpu (WebGPURenderer). Add ?webgl to the URL to force its WebGL2 path. Pins Rapier 0.19.3 on purpose (0.21 hulls never settle), so it cannot share one Rapier version with impossible-spaces as is.

blocks.name: Impossible spaces (portals)
blocks.what: Portals: join any two rectangular openings and look, walk and throw through them. Rooms bigger inside than out, loops, a door onto a wall, a door that shrinks you to a tenth. The system is one file, src/lib/portals.ts.
blocks.good_for: Puzzle and exploration games built on impossible architecture; non-Euclidean levels; surprise moments.
blocks.not_for: Browsers without WebGPU; games that only need a simple teleport (a fade and a position change is enough).
blocks.how_to_add: node tools/blocks/add.mjs impossible-spaces

built_on.name: Wood Floor, Brushed Concrete 04, Marble 01, Black Painted Planks
built_on.by: Dimitrios Savva, Amal Kumar, Rob Tuytel (Poly Haven)

blocks.notes: Needs WebGPU (recent Chrome or Edge). Rendered fine in headless Chromium with WebGPU on.

blocks.name: Grass you can touch
blocks.what: A meadow to the horizon that reacts and remembers: grass bends under feet and anything rolling on it, a scythe mows it and lays the stems in rows, fire spreads with the wind and leaves black ground. A map under it records every touch for your game to read.
blocks.good_for: Outdoor games where the ground matters: mowing, farming, wildfire, tracking, hiding in grass.
blocks.not_for: Indoor games; top-down or high cameras; WebGPU renderers; stylised flat looks without grass; very weak hardware.
blocks.how_to_add: node tools/blocks/add.mjs touch-grass

built_on.name: Blade arc model (maths followed, no file copied)

blocks.name: Realistic procedural dungeons
blocks.what: Seeded crypts to walk in first person: vaulted halls, carved columns, sunken basins, worn paving, stairs through arches, candlelight and deep shadow. The layout comes as plain data with room roles and a path grid.
blocks.good_for: Dark first-person dungeon crawlers, horror, stealth; any game that needs many different dark interiors from a seed.
blocks.not_for: Bright or stylised looks; weak laptops and phones (tested on a fast graphics card only); rooms come empty, you fill them.
blocks.how_to_add: node tools/blocks/add.mjs realistic-procedural-dungeons

built_on.name: Dirt floor, medieval blocks, medieval wall textures

blocks.name: Fire
blocks.what: Real 3D flames made only in shader math (a ray-marched volume): candle, torch, gas jet, campfire, brazier, fireplace, bonfire, burning crate, fire line, with sparks, smoke and a flickering light in sync. No image files.
blocks.good_for: Any game with fire you can walk around and lean into: camps, torches, braziers, burning props.
blocks.not_for: Huge wildfires across a landscape (use many cheap sprites instead); flat 2D or pixel games; WebGPU renderers or orthographic cameras. Note: it draws the frame itself through its FireLayer (see HOW-TO-USE.md).
blocks.how_to_add: node tools/blocks/add.mjs fire
blocks.notes: Inspired by a post by @majidmanzarpour showing volumetric fire in pure three.js; no code came from it.

blocks.name: Realistic car
blocks.what: A car on Rapier at real scale and gravity: tyres that build grip, peak and let go, visible suspension, engine and gearbox, handbrake, and tarmac, gravel and grass. Give it any model with separate wheels.
blocks.good_for: Driving, rally and delivery games that should feel physical; a car to drop into an open world.
blocks.not_for: Arcade kart feel (it is a simulation; tune it down or use a simpler model), 2D games.
blocks.how_to_add: node tools/blocks/add.mjs car

built_on.name: Godot Easy Vehicle Physics (gearbox, suspension, assists, ported)
built_on.by: David Shoemaker, Dechode and Baron Wittman

blocks.name: Destruction physics
blocks.what: Breakable structures on the GPU: a timber barn, a steel water tower, a brick wall and a chimney, each hundreds of rigid pieces welded together, knocked down piece by piece by cannonballs. Welds break by load, so things fall the way they should.
blocks.by: Patch (patch.gg), on three-avbd by Steven Bobyn
blocks.good_for: Demolition, siege and catapult games; physics sandboxes; big satisfying collapses.
blocks.not_for: Browsers without WebGPU; phones; games that only need a few boxes to fall (use Rapier). Its physics is z-up; the starter is y-up.
blocks.how_to_add: node tools/blocks/add.mjs destruction

built_on.name: three-avbd (GPU rigid bodies, copy in vendor/three-avbd)
Sounds: Freesound, Wikimedia Commons and Kenney recordings (some CC-BY-4.0: credit each one)
built_on.by: listed one by one in CREDITS.txt

blocks.notes: art_license is CC-BY-4.0 because some sounds need a credit line: copy the matching lines from CREDITS.txt into my-game/CREDITS.md if those sounds ship.

blocks.name: Crowds and navigation
blocks.what: Make enemies and crowds walk around any three.js level: build a navmesh from its meshes, spawn people, give them a goal; they flow around walls and each other and re-route when something lands in the way. Small API in metres, groups that arrive and stand, milling, walk/run blending, instanced mannequins.
blocks.by: Patch (patch.gg), on recast-navigation-js by Isaac Mason
blocks.good_for: Enemies that chase, townsfolk, armies, herds, tower-defence paths; any game where many characters must find their way.
blocks.not_for: One or two characters on open flat ground (simple steering is enough); thousands of agents; 2D grid games (use a grid A*).
blocks.how_to_add: node tools/blocks/add.mjs crowds
blocks.notes: Its upstream package-lock.json was out of sync with package.json (npm ci failed); we regenerated it with npm install. Nothing else changed.

blocks.name: pixelfx (pixel art effects)
blocks.what: 244 pixel art effects, each a small piece of code drawing into a low-resolution frame: fire, explosions, magic, hits, weather, pickups, UI, critters, and 12 whole acted-out moves. Recolour with palettes, mirror, reseed, export sprite sheets. Includes a Claude Code skill for making new ones.
blocks.good_for: Pixel art and retro games (canvas, Phaser, PixiJS, Kaplay); pixel-style effects on a three.js game via a CanvasTexture or an overlay canvas.
blocks.not_for: Smooth realistic 3D effects (use fire, Effekseer or Ultra Elements).
blocks.how_to_add: node tools/blocks/add.mjs pixelfx

built_on.name: Pixel art VFX method and some effects (adapted)
Fonts in gallery/
built_on.by: Red Hat Project Authors; Funnel Project Authors

blocks.name: EZ-Tree (procedural trees)
blocks.what: Grows a procedural tree in three.js: oak, ash, aspen, pine or bush, from a preset, a seed and about 50 options, swaying in the wind.
blocks.art_license: MIT (leaf textures); bark in Patch's copy is ambientCG CC0
blocks.good_for: Natural-looking trees for outdoor games; making a few tree variants to bake into models.
blocks.not_for: Low-poly or flat looks (see lowpoly-tree-generator); thousands of unique trees at runtime (bake a few, instance them).
blocks.how_to_add: node tools/blocks/add.mjs ez-tree  (clones https://github.com/dgreenheck/ez-tree at the pinned commit into my-game/vendor/ez-tree/; read its README first)

also_see.label: Patch's Tree generator demo (block controls around ez-tree)

blocks.name: Lowpoly Tree Generator
blocks.what: Faceted low-poly trees from six archetypes (about 1,500 triangles, vertex colours, no textures), rigged so a tree can walk, jump, stomp and swing.
blocks.good_for: Low-poly stylised worlds; a tree character; quick forests that match Kenney-style assets.
blocks.not_for: Realistic looks (see ez-tree).
blocks.how_to_add: node tools/blocks/add.mjs lowpoly-tree-generator  (clones https://github.com/pajama-studio/lowpoly-tree-generator at the pinned commit into my-game/vendor/lowpoly-tree-generator/; read its README first)
blocks.preview_note: still from Patch's game-ready demo of this project

also_see.label: Patch's Low-poly trees demo (an island and a walking tree)

blocks.name: threejs-nanites (forests at scale)
blocks.what: A WebGPU renderer that draws any tree a million times: culling, impostors, wind, shadows, temporal upscaling and an auto-quality budget, with forest floor, grass, sky and terrain around it.
blocks.good_for: Huge forests and open worlds in a WebGPU game.
blocks.not_for: The starter's WebGL renderer; phones; small scenes where plain instancing is enough.
blocks.how_to_add: node tools/blocks/add.mjs nanite-forests  (clones https://github.com/VictorZakharov/threejs-nanites at the pinned commit into my-game/vendor/nanite-forests/; read its README first)
blocks.preview_note: still from Patch's game-ready demo of this project

also_see.label: Patch's Forests at scale (baked ez-tree and low-poly trees, planting, trunk collision, a walker)

blocks.name: Three.js Particle Fluids
blocks.what: Liquid, jelly, cloth and smoke as GPU particles (position-based fluids in WebGPU compute shaders); liquid, jelly and cloth push on each other.
blocks.good_for: Pouring, sloshing, gooey or cloth toys; a liquid puzzle; a showpiece effect.
blocks.not_for: The starter's WebGL renderer; phones; big oceans (see ultra-water).
blocks.how_to_add: node tools/blocks/add.mjs particle-fluids  (clones https://github.com/dgreenheck/threejs-particle-fluids at the pinned commit into my-game/vendor/particle-fluids/; read its README first)
blocks.preview_note: still from Patch's game-ready demo of this project

also_see.label: Patch's Particle physics demo (scenes and pointer interaction)

blocks.name: procedural-animals
blocks.what: 24 real animals built, rigged and furred entirely in code: createAnimal('wolf'), add it to the scene and steer it. Gaits, actions (attack, sleep, eat, die) and footstep/hit events. Has an llms.txt written for agents.
blocks.good_for: Wildlife, hunting, herding, safari or farm games; creatures without any model files.
blocks.not_for: Cartoon or low-poly looks without restyling; hundreds of animals at once on weak hardware.
blocks.how_to_add: node tools/blocks/add.mjs procedural-animals  (clones https://github.com/majidmanzarpour/threejs-procedural-animals at the pinned commit into my-game/vendor/procedural-animals/; read its README first)
blocks.preview_note: still from Patch's game-ready demo of this project

also_see.label: Patch's Animals demo (a wolf pack on a hill, with a faster worker build)

blocks.name: Ultra-Water (ocean)
blocks.what: A real-time FFT ocean: shore breakers, foam, caustics, an underwater view with sun shafts, a sky with clouds.
blocks.good_for: Sailing, fishing, island and beach games; anything with a lot of water on screen.
blocks.not_for: Stylised flat water (a simple shader is cheaper); phones.
blocks.how_to_add: node tools/blocks/add.mjs ultra-water  (clones https://github.com/Humpalumps/Ultra-Water at the pinned commit into my-game/vendor/ultra-water/; read its README first)
blocks.preview_note: still from Patch's game-ready demo of this project

also_see.label: Patch's Ocean demo (eight scenes, buoyancy read from the GPU waves, a drivable boat)

blocks.name: Ultra Elements (spell VFX)
blocks.what: 39 real-time elemental spells (fire, ice, lightning, wind, water, earth, void, light, acid, arcane), each simulated on the GPU and tunable.
blocks.good_for: Magic, wizard and action games that need big readable spells.
blocks.not_for: Pixel or flat looks (see pixelfx).
blocks.how_to_add: node tools/blocks/add.mjs ultra-elements  (clones https://github.com/Humpalumps/ultra-elements at the pinned commit into my-game/vendor/ultra-elements/; read its README first)
blocks.preview_note: still from Patch's game-ready demo of this project

also_see.label: Patch's Elements demo (a smaller page and a library around it)

blocks.name: Effekseer for WebGL (+ CC0 sample effects)
blocks.what: Plays particle effects made in the free Effekseer editor inside three.js. The editor ships stylised fantasy sample effects (fire, water, lightning, slashes, heals, shields, hits) under CC0.
blocks.by: Effekseer Project (sample effects: Pierre, NextSoft, AndrewFM, Suzuki, tktk and contributors)

also.what: the editor; its Sample folder (in the editor release) has the CC0 sample effects

blocks.good_for: Stylised fantasy combat effects made by effect artists; teams that want to author effects in an editor.
blocks.not_for: Realistic fire or smoke; pixel games.
blocks.how_to_add: node tools/blocks/add.mjs effekseer  (clones https://github.com/effekseer/EffekseerForWebGL at the pinned commit into my-game/vendor/effekseer/; read its README first)
blocks.preview_note: still from Patch's game-ready demo of this project

also_see.label: Patch's Effekseer effects demo (33 sample effects wired into three.js)

blocks.name: Eanpa Sky (stylised sky)
blocks.what: A volumetric sky and weather engine for three.js WebGPU (TSL): soft painted-looking cumulus, time of day, morphing weather, cloud shadows.
blocks.good_for: Outdoor games with a soft, painterly sky and changing weather.
blocks.not_for: The starter's WebGL renderer as-is (Patch's one-file rewrite also runs on WebGL 2, see also_see).
blocks.how_to_add: node tools/blocks/add.mjs eanpa-sky  (clones https://github.com/SkyeShark/Eanpa-Sky at the pinned commit into my-game/vendor/eanpa-sky/; read its README first)
blocks.preview_note: still from Patch's game-ready demo of this project

also_see.label: Patch's Stylised sky: the sky lifted into one file (src/stylised-sky.js) that also runs on the WebGL 2 fallback and loads in about 2 s

blocks.name: webgpu-skyscape (volumetric clouds and atmosphere)
blocks.what: Real volumetric clouds with cloud shadows and light shafts, a day-night cycle with sun, moon and stars, and aerial haze.
blocks.by: nagoya0, porting takram's three-clouds and three-atmosphere (Shota Matsuda)

also.what: the original clouds and atmosphere (npm @takram/three-clouds, @takram/three-atmosphere) by Shota Matsuda and takram

blocks.good_for: Flight games and big realistic outdoor skies.
blocks.not_for: Stylised looks; weak hardware; the starter's WebGL renderer.
blocks.how_to_add: node tools/blocks/add.mjs skyscape-clouds  (clones https://github.com/nagoya0/webgpu-skyscape at the pinned commit into my-game/vendor/skyscape-clouds/; read its README first)
blocks.preview_note: still from Patch's game-ready demo of this project

also_see.label: Patch's Clouds and sky (flattened from a planet flight demo to a game world you stand in)

blocks.name: GeometryPainterThreeJS
blocks.what: Drag across any mesh and geometry grows along the stroke: quartz crystals, molten cracks, aurora silk, a glowing reef. Instanced and animated in shaders.
blocks.good_for: Magic "painting" mechanics, crystal growth, corruption spreading over a surface; level dressing.
blocks.not_for: The starter's WebGL renderer as-is (it uses three/webgpu with a WebGL 2 fallback).
blocks.how_to_add: node tools/blocks/add.mjs geometry-painter  (clones https://github.com/achrefelouafi/GeometryPainterThreeJS at the pinned commit into my-game/vendor/geometry-painter/; read its README first)
blocks.preview_note: still from Patch's game-ready demo of this project

also_see.label: Patch's Geometry painter (even strokes at any speed, shared instance pools, painting from code)

blocks.name: Elemental Sandbox abilities (August and September)
blocks.what: Character abilities with ground aim indicators, decals, lights, particles and camera shake: Frost Lance, Storm Lance, Cinder Fall, Nova Beam, Voltaic Snare, Glacial Crown (September), plus the August set.

also.what: the August sandbox: Pyre Crown, Kraken Crown, Electrical Sphere, Earthen Spire, Verdant Gate, Tidewrought Ring, Fire Portal, three boosts

blocks.good_for: Action RPGs, MOBA-style or top-down casters that need aimed abilities.
blocks.not_for: Pixel or flat looks.
blocks.how_to_add: node tools/blocks/add.mjs elemental-abilities  (clones https://github.com/achrefelouafi/LinearAbiltyCastingThreeJS at the pinned commit into my-game/vendor/elemental-abilities/; read its README first)
blocks.preview_note: still from Patch's game-ready demo of this project

also_see.label: Patch's Elemental abilities (both sandboxes in one scene, code unedited)

blocks.name: Elemental Sandbox (October): cinematic spells and ragdolls
blocks.what: Five 6 to 12 second spell set pieces that act on real bodies: chains, lightning, roots, crystals and falling planets pin, tear and slice ragdolls (its own position-based solver, no physics engine).
blocks.art_license: MIT; one model ("Magical gyroscope" by reddification) is CC-BY-4.0
blocks.good_for: Finishers, boss moves, spectacle moments in a magic game.
blocks.not_for: Quick everyday attacks (too long); games without humanoid targets.
blocks.how_to_add: node tools/blocks/add.mjs cinematic-spells  (clones https://github.com/achrefelouafi/AbilityCastingThreeJS at the pinned commit into my-game/vendor/cinematic-spells/; read its README first)
blocks.preview_note: still from Patch's game-ready demo of this project

also_see.label: Patch's Cinematic spells (on Patch's CC0 mannequin)

blocks.name: Soil Studio (GrassSystemThreeJS)
blocks.what: Shader soil with mounds, moss, cracks and damp patches under about 200,000 wind-blown grass blades in one draw, with volumetric mist.
blocks.good_for: A beautiful patch of ground: gardens, farms, small outdoor arenas.
blocks.not_for: Ground that reacts to the player (see touch-grass); huge terrains.
blocks.how_to_add: node tools/blocks/add.mjs soil-and-grass  (clones https://github.com/achrefelouafi/GrassSystemThreeJS at the pinned commit into my-game/vendor/soil-and-grass/; read its README first)
blocks.preview_note: still from Patch's game-ready demo of this project

also_see.label: Patch's Soil and grass (a painted field for where grass grows, an earth slab, a CPU height copy so things stand on it)

blocks.name: Pixel Plays (isometric pixel dioramas)
blocks.what: Small browser games as isometric pixel dioramas: describe a ground, place boxes, spheres, trees and people, and get hue-shifted light, dither, hard shadows and wind. No build step, no dependencies. Five small games included.
blocks.art_license: MIT (code-drawn); its music tracks are not licensed for reuse
blocks.good_for: Cosy isometric pixel games; tiny sports or puzzle games; a distinct pixel look without sprites.
blocks.not_for: Full 3D games; reusing its music (generated, not licensed for reuse).
blocks.how_to_add: node tools/blocks/add.mjs pixel-plays  (clones https://github.com/amirmushichge/pixel-plays at the pinned commit into my-game/vendor/pixel-plays/; read its README first)
blocks.preview_note: still from Patch's game-ready demo of this project

also_see.label: Patch's Pixel dioramas (the engine tidied into one function, a turnable sun, wind strength, times of day)

blocks.name: three-voxel-destruction
blocks.what: Teardown-style voxel destruction on the GPU: buildings of thousands of voxel bodies that really fall when what holds them up is knocked out; a chunk graph finds what no longer stands.
blocks.good_for: Voxel demolition and siege games.
blocks.not_for: Browsers without WebGPU; phones; smooth-mesh destruction (see destruction).
blocks.how_to_add: node tools/blocks/add.mjs voxel-destruction  (clones https://github.com/sbobyn/three-voxel-destruction at the pinned commit into my-game/vendor/voxel-destruction/; read its README first)
blocks.preview_note: still from Patch's game-ready demo of this project

also_see.label: Patch's Voxel destruction (a town block, a stone bridge and a house; fixes and look from its game Brickfall)

blocks.name: three-avbd (GPU rigid-body physics)
blocks.what: Augmented Vertex Block Descent (SIGGRAPH 2025) rigid bodies solved in WebGPU compute shaders, with breakable joints. The physics under the destruction block.
blocks.good_for: Thousands of stacked or jointed bodies on the GPU.
blocks.not_for: Ordinary game physics (Rapier is simpler and runs everywhere).
blocks.how_to_add: node tools/blocks/add.mjs three-avbd  (clones https://github.com/sbobyn/three-avbd at the pinned commit into my-game/vendor/three-avbd/; read its README first)

also_see.label: Our vendored destruction block uses it

blocks.name: recast-navigation-js (navmesh and crowds)
blocks.what: Navmesh building, pathfinding and crowd simulation in the browser, with three.js helpers (@recast-navigation/three).
blocks.by: Isaac Mason (WebAssembly port of Recast and Detour by Mikko Mononen, Zlib)
blocks.good_for: Any game where characters must find their way around a 3D level.
blocks.not_for: Grid-based 2D games (a grid A* is simpler).
blocks.how_to_add: node tools/blocks/add.mjs recast-navigation  (clones https://github.com/isaac-mason/recast-navigation-js at the pinned commit into my-game/vendor/recast-navigation/; read its README first)

also_see.label: Our vendored crowds block wraps it in a small game API

blocks.name: ProceduralTerrains
blocks.what: Whole worlds from a seed: volcanic coasts, islands, snowy peaks, canyons, dunes, with water, clouds, erosion and an infinite or planet mode.
blocks.art_license: optional texture pack: Poly Haven and ambientCG, CC0
blocks.good_for: Flying, strategy, island and far-away land seen from the air.
blocks.not_for: First-person ground: up close it is smooth and blurry, with no grass, rocks or trees. Skip its GPL-3 Blender plugin if you copy the repo.
blocks.how_to_add: node tools/blocks/add.mjs procedural-terrains  (clones https://github.com/ZyFou/ProceduralTerrains at the pinned commit into my-game/vendor/procedural-terrains/; read its README first)
blocks.preview_note: still from Patch's game-ready demo of this project

also_see.label: Patch's Terrain (a wrapper with a sky, haze, preset worlds, height reading and a faster load)

blocks.name: Dungeon Forge (procedural dungeons)
blocks.what: Deterministic seeded dungeons: rooms with roles (entrance, combat, elite, treasure, shrine, boss), corridors that connect them, five themes, a geometry kit, liquids, particles and post-processing.
blocks.good_for: Roguelikes and dungeon crawlers; any game that needs a new level layout per run.
blocks.not_for: Realistic stone crypts (see realistic-procedural-dungeons); outdoor levels.
blocks.how_to_add: node tools/blocks/add.mjs dungeon-forge  (clones https://github.com/majidmanzarpour/threejs-procedural-dungeon at the pinned commit into my-game/vendor/dungeon-forge/; read its README first)
blocks.preview_note: still from Patch's game-ready demo of this project

also_see.label: Patch's Dungeons (generator split from the view so you get plain data and a grid for any game, plus a first-person walk)

blocks.name: 00GameDevs magic VFX starter pack
blocks.what: Five magic effects by their author (Darkchain Sigil Rupture, Rift-Shattering Slashes, Luminous Vortex Black Hole, Golden Chain Rain, Sacred Relic Descent), one ES module each with createVFX(options), update(dt), stop(), dispose(). Needs three 0.187 and WebGL2.
blocks.good_for: Big flashy magic moments in a three.js game; the author's site has a larger free catalog with an agent integration guide.
blocks.not_for: Pixel or flat looks; many effects on screen at once on weak hardware.
blocks.how_to_add: node tools/blocks/add.mjs 00gamedevs-vfx  (clones https://git.patch.gg/00vchannel/00gamedevs-vfx-starter.git at the pinned commit into my-game/vendor/00gamedevs-vfx/; read its README first)
blocks.preview_note: the author's own effect previews
blocks.notes: This repo is the author's own release (not a Patch remake). The author's site guide asks agents to report downloads to their API; that is optional and not needed when you take the files from this repo.

blocks.name: trompe (paint a grey level with image models)
blocks.what: Textures a whole grey blockout level with image models: plans cameras where a player can stand, paints what each sees, projects and bakes one texture lit by a real sun, glTF out. Paid image calls on your own key.
blocks.good_for: Realistic buildings seen from a few metres or more; trailers; a first look at a level before real art.
blocks.not_for: Stylised looks; ground at a first-person player's feet; anyone with a $0 generation budget (it makes paid calls: ask the user first).
blocks.how_to_add: node tools/blocks/add.mjs trompe  (clones https://github.com/patch-gg/trompe at the pinned commit into my-game/vendor/trompe/; read its README first)
blocks.preview_note: still from Patch's game-ready demo of this project
blocks.notes: A big tool (about 50 MB repo), not vendored. Clone it at the pinned commit if the user wants it and has agreed to the cost.

blocks.name: anymove (motion capture for any creature from one AI video)
blocks.what: Turns one AI video into a real animation on a creature's own skeleton (wings, tails, eight legs): two cameras in one frame, a DINOv2 joint reader, the rig fitted in both views, a GLB out. Python and ML; uses paid video generation.
blocks.good_for: Custom animations for odd creatures that no animation pack covers.
blocks.not_for: Humanoids (free Mixamo-style or Quaternius CC0 clips are easier); a $0 budget; machines without a capable GPU or Python setup.
blocks.how_to_add: node tools/blocks/add.mjs anymove  (clones https://github.com/patch-gg/anymove at the pinned commit into my-game/vendor/anymove/; read its README first)
blocks.preview_note: still from Patch's game-ready demo of this project
blocks.notes: A big Python tool (about 14 MB repo plus model weights), not vendored. Ask the user before any paid video generation.
